sections.h2: Searching and recording in Bell County
sections.html:
Deeds, liens and plats for Bell County go to the County Clerk in Belton. The Property Records/Recordings desk answers at (254) 933-5171. The clerk works from the Bell County Justice Center at 1201 Huey Road, Belton, TX 76513, weekdays from 8 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon, and takes mail at P.O. Box 480 in Belton.

Search the Official Public Records online. The clerk's main page links a SUPERSEARCH tool built on OCR and CountyFusion, along with a Property Fraud Alert sign-up. Owners of a house they seldom visit should spend the few minutes to enroll.

Before you drive to Belton, call the recording desk and confirm the document type and page count so the right fee is in hand. Staff cannot give legal advice or draft a deed, so questions about wording belong with your title company or attorney. Bring a check or card, and note that mailed items should include a return address for the recorded originals.

Mind the cutoff. After 4:30 p.m. the clerk stops accepting that day's business, and on the final business day of a month the stop comes at 4:15 p.m. A month-end Friday closing means the signed original should be with the title company well ahead.

  • Recording desk: (254) 933-5171, plus a deed recordings email address printed on the clerk's page
  • Civil and probate records: (254) 933-5174
  • Plats: an alphabetical and numerical directory on the clerk's site
  • Mailed recordings: Attn: Recording Dept., P.O. Box 480, Belton

A one-page deed runs $10.00: a $5.00 filing fee plus a $5.00 records management fee. Pages after the first that carry visible marks add $4.00 apiece, and every grantor or grantee indexed beyond five adds $0.25. These rates took effect January 1, 2024, following Senate Bill 1612.

No instrument is held or recorded without the right fee, and personal checks from out of state are refused.

sections.h2: What the clerk needs before accepting a document
sections.html:
The clerk takes an original notarized document or a certified copy of the original. Keep a 2 inch margin free for the stamp and instrument number.

The notary step comes from state law: real property conveyances are recordable only when signed and acknowledged, or sworn to, in front of an authorized officer. Leaving the buyer's mailing address off the deed can bring an extra $25 charge, so read that line before signing.

E-recording is limited to the entities named in Local Government Code 195.003, such as attorneys, banks and title companies. Bell County lists these vendors: CSC, EPN eRecording Network, Simplifile, Hopdox and Indecomm Global Services. A homeowner sending a deed to the clerk mails or delivers the paper original.

The county mixes very different land, so a title searcher meets a wide range of paperwork: old farm tracts with metes and bounds descriptions, subdivision plats around Killeen and Temple, lakefront parcels, and homes near the military post in the western part of the county. The county had an estimated 402,248 residents in mid-2025, 8.5 percent above the 2020 base. Of its 165,094 housing units, 56.5 percent are lived in by their owners. A typical owned home is valued at $241,000, and typical rent is $1,224.

Value is the job of the Bell Central Appraisal District. The clerk only records the deed. Three public offices serve owners: Belton at 411 E. Central (254-939-5841), Killeen at 301 Priest Dr. (254-634-9752) and Temple at 205 E. Central (254-771-1108). Each stays open weekdays until 4:45 p.m., and mail for all three goes to P.O. Box 390 in Belton.

Send deed and address-change questions to the mapping email on its contact page. After a sale this is the step that updates the owner of record, since the district relies on the recorded deed. Protests have their own address, and the district says protests will not be accepted at any other inbox.

Each appraisal reflects who owns the property and its condition on January 1. Homestead notices go out around April 1. To protest, file by May 15 or within 30 days of the notice arriving, whichever is later. School districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead's value, with a further $60,000 for owners 65 and up or disabled.

sections.h2: How records affect a house sale
sections.html:
Any claim recorded against the house appears in the title search and can hold up closing until it is paid off or released. A lien for each year's tax arises on January 1, and the person who owned the house that day remains liable for the bill after a sale.

Here is how a typical recording goes at the Belton office. The signed, notarized deed reaches the recording desk by mail, hand delivery or an approved vendor. Staff check the notary block and the margin, total the fees by page count, and stamp the instrument with its number. The district then picks up the ownership change from the recorded deed. Keep a copy of the stamped pages, because a lender or future buyer will ask for it.

Foreclosure is visible in the same records. A sale notice goes up at the courthouse, with a copy filed at the clerk's office at least 21 days beforehand. The auction itself takes place on the first Tuesday of the month between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. The clerk's schedule lists foreclosure postings at $2.00 when the trustee does it and $12.00 when the clerk posts.

Inherited houses add another layer. Heirs often file an affidavit of heirship, a sworn statement kept by the clerk, though no buyer or lender has to rely on it. A deed that transfers property at death has to be recorded while the owner is alive, and a muniment of title order and will go to the clerk where the land lies.

  • Unpaid taxes, old mortgages and judgments need payoff letters before closing
  • Missing heirs or an unprobated will can stop a title company from insuring
  • A plat or survey mismatch is fixed by a corrective instrument that gets recorded

A cash sale skips the lender, but the title search and the recording still happen. Ask the title company which of these items apply before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: What does Bell County charge to file a single-page deed?
faqs.a: It costs $10.00, split into a $5.00 filing fee and a $5.00 records management fee. Each added page with visible marks is $4.00, and names indexed beyond five are $0.25 each.

faqs.q: Can homeowners e-record in Bell County?
faqs.a: Only qualified filers can. Local Government Code 195.003 limits it to groups such as attorneys, banks and title companies, working through vendors the clerk names. A homeowner mails or hand-delivers the notarized original in Belton.

faqs.q: When does the clerk stop taking recordings each day?
faqs.a: Business for the day ends at 4:30 p.m., or 4:15 p.m. on a month's last business day, so deliver month-end closing documents early.

faqs.q: Where can I order a certified copy of a deed?
faqs.a: Call the clerk's recording desk, (254) 933-5171. Certified copies run $1.00 plus $1.00 a page; plain copies are $1.00 a page.

faqs.q: Who handles questions about my valuation?
faqs.a: The Bell Central Appraisal District does. Its Belton line is 254-939-5841, Killeen is 254-634-9752 and Temple is 254-771-1108.
